extracted.intended_audience: students, UPSC aspirants, policy enthusiasts, civil society actors and readers interested in Indian legislative process and reform
extracted.subtask_description: Explanation and recommended standards for the Pre-Legislative Consultation Framework in India: existing 2014 PLCP requirements, identified weaknesses, and proposed statutory reforms (LIA/PIA, sunset clauses, committee scrutiny, public comments handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public placement period for draft proposals (PLCP 2014)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 2014 Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy (PLCP), the Union Government is required to place legislative proposals (Bills, Rules, Regulations etc.) in the public domain for a period of at least 30 days before they are submitted to the Cabinet for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-day public consultation window is the baseline timing requirement; the piece notes many drafts fail to meet this timeline and that 227 of 301 Bills were presented without prior consultation since the PLCP's introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory accompanying brief with specified contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each draft proposal must be accompanied by a brief note justifying its necessity and covering: (a) financial implications; (b) impact on the environment; (c) impact on the Fundamental Rights of the people; (d) the social and financial costs of the Bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This brief is intended to provide decision-makers and the public with concise information on rationale and consequences; the blog reproduces the PLCP's list as required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comments: summarization and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received from the public need to be summarized and placed on the website of the Department or the Ministry concerned and included in a note to the Cabinet along with the draft proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice should ensure transparency about what feedback was received and how it was considered; current practice often omits such summaries or justification for excluding suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary Committee scrutiny of Bills
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Bill is introduced in a House of Parliament the Presiding Officer can refer it to the appropriate Parliamentary Committee for detailed deliberation; committee examination is a primary mechanism for legislative scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee scrutiny can be time-consuming but allows detailed examination (example: surrogacy Bill took 5 years to examine). The post notes that referral is not mandatory and many Bills bypass committees (only ~25% referred in 16th Lok Sabha). Strengthening scrutiny implies increasing referral rates or making scrutiny obligatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to follow pre-legislative procedures (make consultation mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: The current system is non-obligatory; the blog recommends that Pre-legislative Consultation be made mandatory for all Bills, with narrowly tailored exceptions for urgent legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making consultation mandatory would address the widespread presentation of Bills without prior consultation (noted: 75% of Bills presented without consultation since 2014) and improve deliberative quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government obligation to justify exclusion of suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Government does not accept the recommendations of a Standing/Select Committee, then the Minister in charge of the Bill must submit a memorandum to Parliament explaining the reasons for rejecting such recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a proposed amendment to the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha to increase executive accountability and transparency about decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation Impact Analysis (LIA) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Legislation and Expenditure Accountability Bill, 2022 requires a Legislation Impact Analysis (LIA) report which must offer an assessment of potential costs and benefits to society, the objectives of the intervention with clear measurable outcomes, and the experience of other countries, among other things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LIA is a technical assessment intended to ground law-making in evidence and comparative experience; it should define measurable outcomes so later evaluation is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheme impact analysis for public schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding to LIA for laws, public schemes should have a scheme impact analysis that assesses costs, benefits and defined objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats schemes similarly to statutes so that policy instruments other than laws are also subjected to ex ante scrutiny and measurable goal-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Implementation Assessment (PIA) with three aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIA has three aspects: (a) Performance measurement — evaluates schemes and laws against the objectives defined in the LIA; (b) Impact assessment — evaluates qualitative aspects like social, environmental and legal effects and spillovers; (c) Perception surveys — measure people’s satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIA provides an ex post check to measure whether objectives were achieved, to capture unintended effects, and to record public perception; it complements the LIA and forms a feedback loop for policy improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunset clauses / expiry dates for laws and schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bill requires laws and schemes to have expiry dates (sunset clauses) so the Legislature has an opportunity to re-make laws and schemes and keep them up to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sunset clauses institutionalize periodic review; the Bill further proposes automatic repeal if a law or scheme fails its PIA test in three consecutive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic repeal on repeated PIA failure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a law or scheme fails its PIA test in three consecutive reviews, it would automatically be repealed under the proposed Bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a fail-safe mechanism designed to remove ineffective or harmful measures that persistently fail to meet their defined objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of cost-benefit and net-benefit maximization
rubrics_metrics.description: An effective Pre-Legislative Consultation Framework should ensure any law or scheme is based on the principle that its benefits outweigh the costs and that among alternatives the chosen one confers maximum net benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normative standard underpins the LIA and decision-making — ex ante assessment should compare alternatives and select the option with highest net social benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional capacity and new mechanisms for evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed reforms demand considerable effort by the Executive to undertake proper evaluations; the Bill can lay the groundwork for a new institutional mechanism to ensure self-probity in public expenditure and law-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implementation requires resources, trained staff, and possibly new bodies or units to carry out LIA/PIA and sustain regular monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of media and civil society in strengthening consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Media should do constructive reporting of legislative functioning and enlighten the masses about probable impacts of proposed legislation; civil society groups can support stakeholders in raising their voices in a structured and impactful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent reporting and organized civil society participation are recommended complementary actors to improve public engagement and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder conduct: aim for compromise and consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Impacted stakeholders of any legislative Bill need to sideline their rigid opinions and ideologies in order to build consensus with fellow stakeholders and the Government; policy-making is an exercise in compromise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages stakeholders to engage constructively during consultation rather than adopt maximalist or obstructive postures that impede deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent executive dominance through stronger consultation and scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: A robust Pre-Legislative Consultation Framework is desired to control Executive dominance (especially when combined with anti-defection laws) and ensure accountability to the Legislature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthening consultation and committee scrutiny are proposed institutional checks to balance Executive power within the legislative process.
